layman_headline: Market fear is easing but no new opportunities are ripe enough to pull the trigger.
layman_explanation: The crypto market is in a 'Fear' state but improving from deeper fear last week. Bitcoin is holding at $64K but faces headwinds from rising Treasury yields and oil prices. Our two current positions — Solana and Chainlink — are roughly flat and still within their trade plans. The swing candidates on our watchlist are either already extended after big runs, crashing with no clear floor, or lacking the technical data needed to make a confident call.
layman_action: Hold current positions in SOL and LINK. Both are within their stop-loss and target ranges. Wait for a clearer setup before adding a third position — patience in fearful markets usually pays off.
expert_reasoning: Reviewing all swing candidates: VELVET is down 30% weekly but RSI at 60 is contradictory (not oversold despite the crash — suggests structural breakdown, not a bounce setup). MON has RSI near 39 which is approaching oversold, but it's below SMA20, lacks MACD data, and is a very low-cap asset with no news catalyst. AKE is up 145% in 7 days — classic pump territory, too risky for entry. VVV is up 24% weekly and 18.7% in 24h — chasing momentum here violates swing discipline. FIL is down 99.7% from ATH and dropping further — no floor visible. WLD down 10.7% today with no catalyst or technical support data. The high BTC dominance at 56.6% is unfavorable for alt positions, and our signal credibility data shows CoinDesk and Blockworks news have been historically misleading. Best action is patience.
risk_factors: Rising Treasury yields (highest since 2007 per CryptoSlate) could trigger broader risk-off selling that drags BTC below $64K support
BTC dominance at 56.6% continues to squeeze alt performance, putting SOL and LINK positions at risk
CoinTelegraph analysis flagging BTC's $64.5K spike as a 'low-volume liquidity trap' suggests potential downside
watch_list: BTC price action around $64K — a break below $62K would signal broader risk-off and threaten both positions
MON RSI approaching 35 with a volume spike would create a legitimate oversold bounce entry
Fear & Greed index trajectory — currently improving from 31 to 41; a move above 50 would support alt positions
market_context: Bitcoin is consolidating at $64K in a market transitioning from deep fear (31) to moderate fear (41). Rising Treasury yields and elevated oil prices are creating headwinds for risk assets, while BTC dominance at 56.6% continues to suppress altcoin performance.
context_banner: Fear is receding but no high-conviction swing setups exist — discipline demands patience over forced entries.

key_signals.description: Fear & Greed improved from 31 to 41 (still Fear), suggesting sentiment stabilization but not yet supportive of aggressive new positions.
MON RSI at 39 is the closest to oversold among candidates, but lacks supporting MACD/volume data to confirm a bounce setup.
BTC's spike to $64.5K characterized as a 'low-volume liquidity trap' — suggests caution on assuming BTC support holds.
Bitcoin facing highest Treasury yield hurdle since 2007 with $22.5B less crypto credit — macro headwind for risk assets.
No swing candidate showed meaningful volume breakout patterns; most lack volume comparison data entirely, reducing conviction in any setup.
